newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tarantino film linked to attack on NZ policeman.
newsitem.headline: Tarantino film linked to attack on NZ policeman.

text.p: The torture and attempted murder of a New Zealand policeman may have been fashioned after a scene from the Quentin Tarantino film "Reservoir Dogs", police said on Wednesday.
"That is one of the lines of inquiry that we are following," detective sergeant Dennis O'Rourke said.
Detective Brent Garner was awakened in his home in the North Island township of Ashhurst early Friday morning by a man who bound and gagged him.
The assailant then tortured Garner, carving what police described as deep criss-cross wounds into his back and neck before dousing him in petrol.
When his attacker left, Garner was able to struggle through an open window, falling out into his backyard seconds before an explosion rocked the house and engulfed it in flames.

Police have so far failed to establish a motive but O'Rourke said they were aware the attack resembled a scene in "Reservoir Dogs" where a policeman is tied to a chair, slashed and soaked in petrol. The film was recently screened on a New Zealand pay-TV channel.
O'Rourke said police were also looking at what appeared to be satanic overtones in the attack.
"Anything is possible. He (the offender) had an educated English accent, so there is that inference that perhaps he was English and perhaps he's a traveller," O'Rourke said.
"The details have been sent to Interpol to distribute to other law enforcement agencies internationally to see if they can assist us on this matter."
The possible link with Tarantino's film has led to calls for censorship of film and television violence.
Member of parliament Nick Smith said he was convinced police were dealing with a copycat crime and called for the government to crack down on violence in broadcasting.
